headline: Follower count is a vanity metric
sub: A 12k creator with a real community outsells a 200k creator with a passive one.
caption_body:
Brands still buy reach. Reach doesn't buy anything back.

The creator with 12k followers whose comments are full of real questions will move more product than the 200k account where every comment is a fire emoji.

Before you book anyone, read their last 20 comment sections.

headline: Most collabs fail before the brief is sent
sub: Not because of the creator. Because nobody agreed what success looked like.
caption_body:
A campaign with no defined outcome can't succeed — it can only 'feel okay'.

Decide upfront: are you buying awareness, content you'll reuse in ads, or direct sales? Each one needs a different creator, a different format and a different measure.

Pick one. Write it down. Then brief.

headline: Your brief is too long
sub: Three lines of intent beat three pages of rules.
caption_body:
The longest briefs produce the most generic content.

When you script every second, you get an ad. When you give a creator the product, the audience and one non-negotiable, you get something their followers actually stop for.

Constrain the message. Free the delivery.

headline: You're briefing creators like employees
sub: They know their audience better than your deck does.
caption_body:
The fastest way to kill a collab is to hand a creator a shot list.

You hired them for a voice that took years to build, then asked them to read your copy. Their audience notices instantly — and engagement tells you so.

Bring the what. Let them own the how.

headline: What a good campaign actually looks like
sub: Brief → shortlist → approve → ship. Four steps, not forty.
caption_body:
Most brands overcomplicate this.

You define the goal and budget. You get a shortlist of creators who fit. You approve the ones you like. They ship.

Everything else — the chasing, the rate haggling, the follow-ups — is admin somebody else should be absorbing.

headline: You're undercharging. Here's the test
sub: If every brand says yes immediately, your rate is too low.
caption_body:
A healthy rate gets pushback sometimes. If nobody has ever hesitated, you've priced yourself below what the market would have paid.

Raise it 20% on the next enquiry. The brands worth working with will still say yes — and you'll stop resenting the ones who don't.

headline: 'We'll pay you in exposure'
sub: Exposure doesn't pay rent, and brands with budgets never open with this.
caption_body:
A brand that can afford product can afford people.

'Great visibility', 'long-term potential', 'we'll feature you' — these are what companies say when they have a marketing budget but haven't allocated any of it to you.

Politely ask for their rate card. Watch what happens.

headline: Your pitch email is about you
sub: Brands don't care about your follower count. They care what it does for them.
caption_body:
Rewrite the opener. Instead of 'I have 40k followers and great engagement', try 'your new launch is aimed at students in Delhi — that's 60% of my audience'.

One is a statistic. The other is a reason to reply.

headline: A media kit doesn't need to be pretty
sub: It needs four numbers and one screenshot.
caption_body:
Creators spend a weekend in Canva and miss the point.

Brands want: audience size, top city, gender split, average reel views — plus one screenshot of your insights so they know you're not making it up.

One page. Send it as a PDF. Done.

headline: Always ask for 50% upfront
sub: Not rude. Standard. Every other freelance industry does it.
caption_body:
You wouldn't ask a photographer to shoot a whole campaign and invoice later, hopefully.

Half before you shoot, half on delivery. Brands that work with creators properly won't blink. The ones that argue are telling you something useful about how the rest of the project will go.
